key_features.classic_presentation: Severe constipation presents with lower abdominal cramping, bloating, straining with bowel movements, hard stools, and sensation of incomplete evacuation. Pain is usually mild-moderate, diffuse. Gradual onset over days to weeks.
key_features.typical_demographics: More common in elderly, females, sedentary lifestyle. Medications (opioids, anticholinergics) are common causes.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Slow colonic transit or defecation disorders lead to hard, infrequent stools.

diagnostic_questions.context: Pain is usually mild-moderate cramping/bloating, not severe.
Often chronic issue, not acute first presentation.
Many medications cause constipation. Opioids are most common.

red_flags.finding: Severe pain with no BM for >7 days
Blood in stool with new-onset constipation
red_flags.action: Rule out malignancy or other serious cause

typical_management: Increase fiber, hydration, exercise. Stool softeners, osmotic laxatives (miralax). Avoid chronic stimulant laxative use.
disposition: Outpatient management unless red flags present.
patient_education: Constipation is very common. Treatment includes dietary changes, fluids, and laxatives if needed. See doctor if it doesn't improve or if you have concerning symptoms.
